text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The paper says the state should create an anti-Mafia institution to deal with Albania's rising crime.
- At the request of the Italian Interpol Albanian police arrested two Italians under investigation for crimes in Turin.

- Following an agreement between the government and the main Independent Trade Union on a wage increase, Azem Hajdari, a ruling party MP and leader of a rival trade union, says they will hold a strike on January 6 1997.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat arrives in Albania for a two-day visit.
- The creation of a commission to monitor pyramid schemes has caused friction within the ruling Democratic party.
- The ongoing strike by the Greek farmers has pushed prices up in neighbouring Albania.
- Albanians have spent some five billion leks on New Year celebrations.
- Alberto Maritati, a senior Italian police official on a visit to Albania, says the Italian Mafia may be depositing its money in Albania.
- Hundreds of people are anxiously waiting to get back their deposits from a notorious pyramid scheme, which has said there would be no returns on the investments.
- The Japanese government has given a grant of $3 million for Albanian agriculture.
- A visit of the Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi to Italy this week was postponed. Albania and Italy were due sign an agreement on emigration and economic cooperation for three years.
